Subject: OrchidAI — post-discovery: ML infra lab (60–90m) & agenda

Hi Alana / Miguel —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion on model performance expectations and the production constraints you highlighted (SLA targets ~100ms P95, strict data residency for logs). As promised, shorthand recap + proposed next step to get your ML and infra teams hands-on: a 60–90 minute technical lab (we'll bring one infra engineer + one ML engineer). Goal: validate serving assumptions, review data flow and security controls, and identify any integration blockers.

Proposed slots (your timezone):
- Tue May 30 — 09:30–11:00 PT
- Wed May 31 — 13:00–14:30 PT
- Thu Jun 1 — 08:00–09:30 PT

Proposed agenda (60–90m):
1) 10 min: quick goals & attendee intros
2) 20–30 min: architecture review (your current infra + Redwood serving/runtime overview)
3) 20–30 min: hands-on walkthrough (sample inference run, KV/prefix cache behavior, batching tradeoffs)
4) 15 min: security & deployment controls (VPC options, KMS, audit logs)
5) 10 min: action items & mutual next steps (rollout options + timeline)

Pre-read attached (short doc) — cover: model size/ops, sample QPS, and data retention constraints. Can you: (a) confirm a preferred slot, (b) share the likely attendees from your side (engineer names + emails), and (c) call out 1–2 highest-priority scenarios you want us to exercise during the lab?

If any of the proposed slots are tight we can expand to a 90-min block — happy to be flexible.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear recap.

We're excited to move forward. Miguel and I chatted with the infra team — the Wed May 31 13:00–14:30 PT slot works best for us. Attendees from OrchidAI: Miguel Santos (infra lead, miguel@orchidai.com) and Priya Kapoor (ML engineering, priya.kapoor@orchidai.com).

Top priorities for the lab:
- Validate end-to-end latency for short text payloads (P95 requirement) and how caching/batching will affect real-time queries.
- Confirm how Redwood's private deployment option fits with our on-prem data retention and KMS setup (we may need client-managed keys).

One question: will you be able to exercise a model that is ~6B parameters and an FP16-like serving profile, or do you want us to provide a sample artifact + weights in advance?

Quick note: we're in a procurement review so we'll also have our procurement contact follow-up separately on terms if the technical fit looks good.
